planets.name: Sun
planets.description: The Sun is the star at the center of our Solar System. It is a nearly perfect sphere of hot plasma, heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion reactions in its core. The Sun radiates energy mainly as light, ultraviolet, and infrared radiation, and is the most important source of energy for life on Earth.
planets.atmosphere: Hydrogen 73.5%, Helium 24.9%, Oxygen, Carbon, Neon, Iron
facts: The Sun accounts for 99.86% of the total mass of the Solar System.
About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old — roughly halfway through its life.
The Sun's surface temperature is about 5,500 °C, but its corona reaches millions of degrees.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.description: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun. Despite being closest to the Sun, it is not the hottest planet — that distinction belongs to Venus. Mercury has no atmosphere to retain heat, causing extreme temperature variations between day and night.
planets.atmosphere: Trace amounts of oxygen, sodium, hydrogen, helium, potassium
facts: Mercury has the most extreme temperature variations of any planet, from -180°C to 430°C.
A day on Mercury (one full rotation) lasts about 59 Earth days.
Mercury has a large iron core, making up about 85% of its radius.
Despite being the closest planet to the Sun, Venus is hotter than Mercury.
Mercury has almost no atmosphere — it has an exosphere made of atoms blasted off its surface.

planets.name: Venus
planets.description: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and the hottest planet in our Solar System. Its thick atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, making it hotter than Mercury. Venus rotates backwards compared to most planets and spins very slowly.
planets.atmosphere: 96.5% CO₂, 3.5% N₂, trace amounts of SO₂, H₂O, Ar
facts: Venus is the hottest planet with surface temperatures around 465°C.
A day on Venus is longer than its year — it takes 243 Earth days to rotate once.
Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most planets — the Sun rises in the west.
The atmospheric pressure on Venus is 90 times greater than on Earth.
Venus is the brightest natural object in Earth's night sky after the Moon.

planets.name: Earth
planets.description: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known world to support life. Its liquid water, oxygen-rich atmosphere, and magnetic field create a stable environment uniquely suited to life. Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System.
facts: Earth's magnetic field deflects harmful solar wind particles.
The Moon stabilises Earth's axial tilt, moderating climate.
About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by liquid water.
Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System (5.51 g/cm³).
The planet is ~4.54 billion years old.

planets.name: Mars
planets.description: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System. Known as the Red Planet due to iron oxide on its surface, Mars has the largest volcano and deepest canyon in the Solar System. Its thin atmosphere and cold climate make it inhospitable to known life.
planets.atmosphere: 95.3% CO₂, 2.7% N₂, 1.6% Ar, trace O₂, H₂O
facts: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest volcano in the Solar System, nearly three times the height of Everest.
Mars has the largest dust storms in the Solar System, lasting months.
A Martian day (sol) is 24 hours and 37 minutes — very similar to Earth.
Mars has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos.
Mars had liquid water on its surface billions of years ago.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.description: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the Solar System. It is a gas giant more than twice as massive as all other planets combined. Jupiter's most famous feature is the Great Red Spot, a storm that has been active for over 350 years.
planets.atmosphere: 89% H₂, 10% He, trace CH₄, NH₃, H₂O, C₂H₂
facts: Jupiter is so large that all other planets in the Solar System could fit inside it.
The Great Red Spot is a storm on Jupiter larger than Earth that has raged for 350+ years.
Jupiter has the fastest rotation of any planet — a day lasts only about 10 hours.
Jupiter has at least 95 known moons, including the four large Galilean moons.
Jupiter acts as a 'cosmic vacuum cleaner', protecting inner planets by capturing asteroids.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.description: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest in the Solar System. It is famous for its stunning ring system made of ice and rock. Saturn is the least dense planet — it would float on water. It has the most extensive moon system in the Solar System.
planets.atmosphere: 96.3% H₂, 3.25% He, trace CH₄, NH₃, HD, C₂H₆
facts: Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice and rock, ranging from tiny grains to objects as large as houses.
Saturn is the least dense planet — its density is less than water.
Saturn has 146 known moons, including Titan, which has a thick nitrogen atmosphere.
Saturn's rings extend up to 282,000 km from the planet but are incredibly thin.
Saturn's moon Titan is larger than the planet Mercury.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.description: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and the third-largest by diameter. It rotates on its side, with an axial tilt of 97.77°, meaning its poles experience 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness. It is composed mostly of ice and rock.
planets.atmosphere: 83% H₂, 15% He, 2.3% CH₄, trace NH₃, HD, C₂H₂
facts: Uranus rotates on its side with an axial tilt of nearly 98°.
Uranus is the coldest planetary atmosphere in the Solar System at -224°C.
Uranus has 13 known rings, which are dark and narrow.
A year on Uranus lasts 84 Earth years.
Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope, by William Herschel in 1781.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.description: Neptune is the eighth and farthest known planet from the Sun. It is an ice giant with the strongest winds in the Solar System, reaching 2,100 km/h. Neptune was predicted mathematically before it was directly observed and was first discovered in 1846.
planets.atmosphere: 80% H₂, 19% He, 1.5% CH₄, trace HD, C₂H₂, C₂H₆
facts: Neptune has the strongest winds of any planet — up to 2,100 km/h.
Neptune was the first planet located through mathematical prediction rather than observation.
A year on Neptune lasts 165 Earth years.
Neptune's moon Triton orbits in the opposite direction to Neptune's rotation.
Neptune has a Great Dark Spot — a storm system like Jupiter's Great Red Spot.

planets.name: Moon
planets.description: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and the fifth-largest in the Solar System. It is the largest and most massive satellite relative to its parent planet in the Solar System. The Moon's gravitational influence creates Earth's tides and has gradually slowed Earth's rotation.
planets.atmosphere: Extremely thin exosphere: Ar, He, Na, K, H, Rn
facts: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at about 3.8 cm per year.
The Moon is in synchronous rotation with Earth — we always see the same side.
The Moon stabilises Earth's axial tilt, keeping climate relatively stable.
Footprints left by Apollo astronauts will last for millions of years — no wind to erase them.
The Moon is the only extraterrestrial body humans have ever visited.
